in_text_mentions: Flexible naso-laryngoscopy revealed normal but paralyzed vocal folds. Unusually she had a soft mass arising from the posterior pharyngeal wall obscuring the view of the posterior commissure and vocal folds. The shape of the mass altered with respiration and on performing valsalva maneuvers (Figure 1). A plain lateral neck radiograph revealed a large air filled sac originating from the laryngeal cartilages and extending along the posterior pharyngeal wall (Figure 2).
